title: Phase 1 Data Accuracy Fixes — productive_sessions, zero-token validation, top_sessions dates
outcome: All 3 Phase 1 data accuracy fixes implemented and verified. 10 new tests added, all 76 tests pass (66 existing + 10 new). No regressions.
key_decisions: Changed productive_sessions formula from max(1, ...) to max(0, ...) to prevent inflation of build session counts on commit dates with negligible build activity
Added _validate_models() as a pure function in merge.py that scans models_data for zero-token anomalies and returns warning messages
Added 'warnings' key to merge_datasets() return dict, populated by _validate_models() output
Added time_created to top_sessions SQL SELECT clause and populated TopSessionRow.created from query result instead of hardcoding empty string
Wrote source-code inspection tests for merge.py and top_sessions.py to verify the fixes are in place (following existing test conventions in the project)
learnings: The existing test test_productive_sessions_at_least_one_per_commit_date_with_build still passes because the build_tok > 0 filter excludes zero-build days before the max() is applied. The max(1) -> max(0) change affects edge cases with very small build ratios.

The project's test convention uses source-code inspection (reading .py files and checking for patterns) alongside functional tests. This is effective for verifying structural changes without needing database fixtures.

The _validate_models function follows the existing pattern of pure helper functions in merge.py (like _build_merged_daily, _build_phases, etc.) — no external dependencies, no side effects beyond logging.
next_steps: Phase 2: Input validation hardening — _resolve_date() rejecting 'None' string and invalid dates
Phase 3: Model pricing completeness — add 4 missing models to MODEL_PRICING
Phase 4: Documentation and disclaimer — cache hit rate clarification in HTML report
Regenerate CollageMaker report to verify productive_sessions is realistic and warnings array includes zero-token models
